title: Cascading failure from overload after a heat wave — July 2026
summary: A grid overload driven by cooling demand triggered a cascading failure that hit several dependent elements in under 10 minutes.
outcome: The repair took 45 minutes because the origin substation was not identified until 15 minutes in. Lesson: when several elements fail almost simultaneously, first check whether they share the same origin substation before treating them as independent incidents.

title: Partial restoration that created a false sense of resolution — March 2026
summary: Grid voltage partially recovered (60%) after a first repair, which led the system to lower the incident's priority before the repair was complete.
outcome: The grid went down again 20 minutes later, creating a second crisis peak. Lesson: do not close or deprioritize a substation incident until grid voltage stays stable above 90% for at least 5 minutes.

title: Crew diverted mid-route by a new priority — May 2026
summary: A crew already en route to the substation was redirected to a hospital by a sudden emergency, delaying the substation repair.
outcome: The substation repair was delayed 22 minutes, prolonging the crisis for every element depending on it. Lesson: diverting a crew heading to the root cause (substation) is only justified if the new destination is more critical than fixing the blackout's origin for everyone else.
